summary: Track 24.8 JobPicker touch-select regression testing on /daily/submit preview. Desktop click and keyboard Enter regressions PASS. Stationary mobile tap PASSES for Oxford (24-12), University High (26-07), and Custom job. HOWEVER the core Track 24.8 fix — the movement-threshold scroll-vs-tap disambiguation — DOES NOT ACTUALLY WORK. Simulated scroll (200px vertical pointermove sequence on the first row) still commits the initial row (verified: label became '20-07 · T5686 SR 15/SR600' after scrolling with pointerdown on 20-07). This is a P0 — the operator's original 'wrong row selected while scrolling' bug is NOT fixed.

ui_bugs.issue: P0: cmdk's CommandItem internally sets its OWN onPointerMove handler AFTER the props spread, which OVERRIDES the onPointerMove from commitHandlersFor(...). Result: touchRef.active is NEVER set to false during a scroll gesture, so onPointerUp still commits the row where the finger first touched down. Track 24.8 movement-cancel logic is a no-op.

integration_issues.issue: Scrolling from row 1 down 200px commits row 1 (label changes to '#20-07'). Expected: no commit, label stays 'Pick a MASCI job — or choose Custom'. This is a reproduction of the original operator complaint on preview.

action_items: URGENT P0: Rewrite commitHandlersFor so its onPointerMove is NOT overridden by cmdk. Options: (a) attach the movement-cancel via useRef + native addEventListener on the CommandItem's underlying DOM node, (b) wrap CommandItem children in an inner <div> that owns the pointer handlers, (c) intercept pointermove on the CommandList/scroll container level, or (d) use pointer capture / scroll-detection based on the scroll container's scroll event.

Verify cmdk 1.x source at /app/frontend/node_modules/cmdk/dist/index.mjs — CommandItem creates its element with `{...q, ..., onPointerMove: A||disable?undefined:S, onClick: C}`. The onPointerMove from spread props is unconditionally overwritten.
Re-run the same simulated-scroll test after fix — it should keep the trigger label as 'Pick a MASCI job — or choose Custom'.
critical_code_review_comments: Track 24.8 fix architectural miss: spreading React event handlers onto a wrapper component (CommandItem) is unsafe when that component sets its own handlers of the same name. cmdk's <Item> overrides onPointerMove; our handler is dropped silently — no TypeScript/lint error since props shape is compatible.

Suggested fix pattern: `const itemRef = useRef(null); useEffect(() => { const el = itemRef.current; if(!el) return; el.addEventListener('pointermove', handler, {passive:true}); return () => el.removeEventListener('pointermove', handler); }, []);` This bypasses React's synthetic layer and cmdk's overrides.
Alternative: listen for scroll on CommandList and set a 'scrolling' flag that pointerup checks.

success_rate.frontend: 67% (4/6 tests pass; stationary tap works but scroll-cancel — the whole point of 24.8 — does not)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview URL: https://backup-forensics.preview.emergentagent.com/daily/submit. Job list has 29 jobs including Oxford (24-12) and University High Parent Loop Ext (26-07). To simulate real touch when the Playwright context lacks has_touch, dispatch PointerEvents via page.evaluate — set pointerType:'touch', bubbles:true, composed:true. Use pointerdown→(20x pointermove increments)→pointerup pattern on a row's DIV via document.elementFromPoint. After fix, the scroll test MUST leave trigger label unchanged.

rca_of_the_issue.symptom: iOS user sees dropdown, taps 'University High School' row, but a DIFFERENT job commits. Also scrolling past a row commits whichever row the finger first touched.
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: cmdk (shadcn Command) <Item> renders `<div ... onPointerMove={S} onClick={C}>` where the onPointerMove and onClick are placed AFTER the {...props} spread. The commitHandlersFor(...) from JobPicker.jsx passes onPointerDown/onPointerMove/onPointerUp via prop spread, but onPointerMove is overwritten by cmdk's internal selection-highlight handler. Therefore the movement-cancel branch (touchRef.current.active = false) never executes. onPointerUp still commits because active is still true, regardless of how far the finger travelled.
reproduction_steps_preview: On the first row (data-testid job-picker-item-20-07) dispatch a synthetic touch pointerdown → 20 pointermove events dropping y by 10px each (total 200px) → pointerup.
Observe trigger label becomes 'T5686 SR 15/SR600 (SANFORD, 17/92, LAKE MARY)  ·  #20-07' — a wrong commit from a pure scroll gesture.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Attach pointermove listener via native addEventListener on the item's DOM node (using a ref), NOT via React prop spread onto CommandItem. Alternatively, detect scroll at the CommandList container and set a shared 'suppressCommit' flag that onPointerUp respects.
